best_score.note: 2026-08-29 alignment pass (coordinator-directed): verified constants against real assembled+objdumped bytes instead of by-eye asm reading, per the 08077428 techique. Method: arm-none-eabi-as/-objdump the three retained .s files standalone, WITH an explicit leading pad matching each function real address mod-4 parity (Fragment_0800f1fa starts at 0x0800f1fa, which is ODD mod4=2, so a naive standalone assembly misaligns its literal pool by one halfword and reads garbage - padding with one leading .short 0 before assembling fixes this). This caught FIVE real bugs a plain source read missed: (1) the speed/accel magnitude constants at the top of the function were off by a factor of 16 (128<<9 is 0x10000, not 0x100000 - the .c had 0x100000/0x180000/0x80000/0x400000/0x200000 where the real shifts produce 0x10000/0x18000/0x4000/0x40000/0x10000); (2) the second Func_080770c0 gate constant is 383 (0x17f, loaded from a literal pool), not 0x2c0/704 - a plain-immediate guess that was never pool-verified; (3) the head Data_03001f54-debug-shortcut (asm 0800ebec.s ~176-190) was implemented but placed BEFORE building posA and calling the first Func_0800447c, when the real asm places it AFTER that call and BEFORE the paired Func_080120dc call - moved to the correct position; (4) the counter-table check near Region_0800ee14 .L_0800f0c6 does NOT read Data_03001e70_a directly - the pool word at that ldr resolves to Data_03001ebc_a, and the value read from Data_03001ebc_a is itself a POINTER that gets indexed as a u16 table (*(u16**)Data_03001ebc_a)[206], not a flat array read - fixed; (5) Fragment_0800f1fa's post-mode-2 flag check (asm .L_0800f294) reads *(actor+102) unconditionally into a local, and ONLY if that value is exactly 2 does it get force-reset to 0 by a literal (confirmed via objdump: the pool word is 0x00000000, not 0x00000001 as the earlier draft guessed) before the final !=0 check that gates the spawned+6 write - restructured to match. Also fixed a real STRUCTURAL bug independent of constant verification: the tail_merge goto target (both the (angle_q16>>16)==0xffff path and the debug-shortcut path jump to sub_0800f0c6) was positioned AFTER the "blocked==0&&handled!=0" actor+48/+52 overwrite block, the Data_03001ebc_a table increment, AND the Func_0800c300 dispatch - meaning both early-exit paths completely skipped the counter-table update and the mode/blocked/handled dispatch call that the real function always performs. Moved tail_merge to land exactly where sub_0800f0c6 sits in the asm (right after the actor+48/+52 block, immediately before the table check), so both early-exit paths now run the dispatch like the reference does. Also replaced the ad-hoc struct-WorldPosition-plus-cast idiom (posX.x=...; *(s32*)posX.unknown_04=...; posX.y=...) with a plain s32[3] local array cast to struct WorldPosition* at each call site, matching the established idiom in games/gs1/recon/en/units/*.c (e.g. 08098698.c) - the cast idiom was making gcc compute the middle-field address as a separate temporary instead of a plain contiguous store, which was visibly adding extra instructions in the --align diff. Net effect: wrong_instructions dropped 825 -> 768 across this pass (825 baseline was BEFORE this session's first structural pass too - see prior note); dh moved 867 -> 871 (a slight regression in raw halfword count, expected/acceptable at this stage since dh is not the right metric before wrong_instructions reaches 0 per the project's own staged methodology). matched_prefix stayed at 7 instructions despite three distinct head-of-function reordering attempts (see entry_order_investigation below) - this appears to be a genuine GCC-2.96-at-O2 list-scheduler artifact tied to whole-function register pressure, not a source-order bug reachable by simple statement reshuffling. NOT byte-exact; do not run make verify.

Total span is roughly 0800ebec-0800f2e0, about 1.8KB. This matches the sibling finding already recorded for 0800ee14 (games/gs1/recon/en/main/0800ee14.json): no ordinary standalone C function can reproduce a mid-function branch target with a live caller-established frame, so 0800ee14/0800ef44/0800f0c6/0800f1fa cannot be scored as separate owners, and 0800ebec cannot be adopted as a 552-byte owner either, because its C body does not actually end at 0800ee14 - it is the same function.

entry_order_investigation: Per coordinator direction, ran bun tools/allocator-lens/lens.ts 0800ebec and cross-referenced the kept GCC dump directory (0800ebec.c compiles with actual staged gcc-2.96 cc1 at -O2, confirmed by reading tools/allocator-lens/lens.ts - this is not a custom allocator, it is real GCC). RTL pseudo 32 = the incoming actor parameter (reg/v:SI 32 <- r0), created by the very first frontend insn (insn 4), BEFORE the blocked_flags/handled_flags zero-stores (insn 12/15) - so the source-level order is already correct at the RTL-generation stage, matching the reference asm. The divergence happens at instruction SCHEDULING (in.i.23.sched2 dump): the list scheduler's block-0 ready list at t=0 is '4 18 12 3459' (insn4=r7:=r0, insn12=first zero-store, insn3459=stack-pointer adjustment, insn18=literal-pool load) and it picks insn3459 then insn12 before finally scheduling insn4 at t=10, right before the branch - i.e. GCC's own priority heuristic ranks the parameter copy LOWER than the stack setup and zero-stores in this specific function shape, even though insn4's result (r7) has by far the largest number of later uses in the function. Tried three source-level nudges and re-scored each: (a) swap store order (handled_flags=0 before blocked_flags=0), (b) combine into one assignment (blocked_flags = handled_flags = 0), (c) hoist a dummy 'base = (u8 *)actor;' statement to the very top. None moved matched_prefix past 7 or changed dh/wrong_instructions at all - GCC's cse/combine passes normalize all three variants to the same RTL before scheduling ever sees them. Conclusion: this specific 7-instruction prefix mismatch is very likely NOT fixable by reshaping these particular statements; it is downstream of the function's overall register-pressure profile (515-535 pseudos observed across drafts, sensitive to total local/temporary count), and probably will resolve on its own once the much larger remaining wrong_instructions gap (768) is closed by content fixes elsewhere - or requires a scheduler-priority lever (e.g. deliberately increasing/decreasing live-range length of the actor parameter by moving its first REAL use earlier) that was not tried this pass due to time.
